definition: A cheaper LayerNorm variant that normalizes by the root mean square without centering the mean.
details: A cheaper LayerNorm variant that normalizes by the root mean square without centering the mean. Used by Llama-family and most modern LLMs for a small speed and stability win.

explainer.lead: RMSNorm is a cheaper LayerNorm variant that normalizes by the root mean square without centering the mean. It is used by the Llama family and most modern LLMs for a small speed and stability win.

tiers.eli5: Like resizing a photo by its overall brightness without first shifting the colors — you get most of the benefit with less work.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers swap it in for LayerNorm in transformer blocks to save compute and stabilize training. A pitfall is assuming it behaves identically to LayerNorm, since it skips mean centering.
tiers.paperLevel: Normalization by the root mean square, without subtracting the mean. Known trade-off: it is a cheaper approximation to LayerNorm rather than an equivalent.

explainer.example: A Llama-style transformer block applies RMSNorm before attention, dividing activations by their root mean square without centering.
